Interactive · click a numbered spot

The Visual plant 3D tab at a glance

The board operator sees tags on a screen. The outside operator walks to them: this tab is that walk.

Every control serves one job: get to the item, read or operate it, and leave a line in the log.

Part 1 · where the plant comes from

Tags, places and values come from three sources

EPC P&ID

SEP-V101-PID-001: tags, line numbers, normal valve positions

Layout

SEP-V101-LA-PLT-001: coordinates, heights, platforms, ladders, route

Model

the running simulator: every reading and valve state

$(x,\,y,\,z)_{\text{3-D view}}=(x_E,\;z_{up},\;-y_N)$

Layout metres: $x_E$ east, $y_N$ north, $z_{up}$ up from grade; the viewer swaps axes.

Interactive · walk the route

Thirteen stations on the plot plan

The round starts at the control room; only two stations are on a platform: up one ladder, down another.

Interactive · pick a line number

From the P&ID line number to the coloured pipe

The line number carries size, service and sequence; the 3-D view paints the service, so a pipe is traced by colour.

Interactive · height above the floor

Can it be read from where you stand?

Of 27 gauges and transmitters, 21 are read from grade; one sits 6.3 m up with no platform beside it.

Interactive · findings recorded in the tab

Where the documents and the 3-D view differ

Each difference is written down with its reason, never smoothed over in the model.

Part 1 · summary

What part 1 settled

  • Tags and valve positions come from the EPC P&ID, places from the layout, values from the model.
  • The round is 13 stations and 231 m; two stations are on the EL +3.7 m platforms.
  • A line number gives size, service and sequence; the service sets the pipe colour.
  • Differences between sources are recorded as open points.

Part 2 · What the outside operator reads

Which field readings tell the truth, and how is the round checked?

Part 2 · the plan

Reading the plant, not the screen

  1. Four kinds of readingtrue process, own indication, stem, state
  2. The vessel gaugesgauge glass, displacer, radar, thermometer
  3. A glass that lieswhat its isolation valves do to the reading
  4. Tolerances and pairswhen a difference is worth reporting
  5. The recordoutlet trains, identification, log lines

Interactive · what a field item shows

Four kinds of reading on 63 field tags

Only seven readings show the process directly; a transmitter shows its own measurement, which can be wrong.

Interactive · click a numbered spot

The level and temperature gauges on V-101

One interface is measured three ways: the glass for the eye, the displacer for control, the radar for the trip.

Virtual lab · the glass and its valves

When does LG-121 show the true interface?

The glass is the operator's reference, but it sees the vessel only through three hand valves.

With an isolation closed the glass keeps the old level while the vessel moves on; trust it only with both isolations open.

Interactive · local against transmitter

Is the difference worth a call to the board?

A difference inside the reading tolerance is reading error; outside it, one of the two instruments is wrong. Values illustrative.

Interactive · click a numbered spot

What the operator checks on the outlet trains

Brown is oil, blue is produced water: follow the colour from the shutdown valve to the meter, analyser and sample point.

Interactive · the 28 rows by kind

The rounds sheet: what is written down

The sheet is checked against the live plant: a number counts only inside its tolerance.

Interactive · what each action writes

Every action on the round leaves a log line

The wording is fixed, so exercises and the Debrief grade the round from the log, not from memory.

Part 2 · summary

What part 2 settled

  • Glasses, local gauges and SIS level transmitters show the process; other transmitters show their own measurement.
  • A gauge glass is true only with both isolations open.
  • Pairs are compared within the reading tolerance.
  • Every read, check and valve move writes a fixed log line.

Part 3 · Hand valves and safe field work

When may the outside operator move a hand valve, and what does it do?

Part 3 · the plan

Forty hand valves, five normal positions

  1. Normal positionsNO, NC, LO, LC, CSO and who may change them
  2. Locks and seals in the fieldwhat they look like in the 3-D view
  3. Valve familieswhere each kind of valve sits and why

Interactive · pick a normal position

The normal position is printed on the P&ID

32 of 40 valves can be moved in the tab; the 8 locked-open or car-sealed valves refuse.

Interactive · click a numbered spot

A lock, a trap and a drain at the heater

The P&ID letters become hardware: a padlock, a car seal, a hand wheel whose colour tells open from closed.

The colour of the wheel and the lock on the stem are read before the tag plate.

Part 3 · the close-up

Operate opens a close-up of the valve

Locked open: the tab refuses the move.

Normally closed: Open and Close work.

Each close-up states the model's effect of moving that valve.

Interactive · pick a family

Where the 40 hand valves sit, and why

The family predicts the normal position: isolations open, drains closed, relief car-sealed open.

Interactive · click a hand valve

Blocks, bypass and battery limit around a control valve

Model, hvTrain$f=(x\,b_1b_2+0.4\,b_p)\,b_L$

A closed block or battery-limit valve stops the train whatever the controller does; an open bypass adds 40 % of the control valve.

Interactive · model runs, valve moved at 1 min

What the board sees when the field moves a valve

The controller hides the move by closing its own valve; the board sees an output change, sometimes an alarm first.

Interactive · before, during, after

Moving a valve safely

General field practice, not a site procedure: agree, move slowly, confirm, restore, record.

Part 3 · summary

What part 3 settled

  • 40 hand valves: 18 NO, 12 NC, 6 LO, 2 LC, 2 CSO, from the EPC P&ID.
  • Locked and car-sealed valves move only under a permit or procedure.
  • Blocks, bypass and battery limit set what a control valve can pass.
  • A field move shows on the board as a controller output change.

This deck

Key Takeaways

1

Find every field item by its P&ID tag and its layout station.

2

Trust a gauge glass only with both isolation valves open.

3

Compare local gauges with transmitters inside the reading tolerance.

4

Check every hand valve against its normal position on the P&ID.

5

Tell the board before and after you move a valve.
